requirements:
Shell-like word splitting, level 1. These rules define a custom language; do not add shell behavior.

R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with rustc --edition 2024, std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. All API types, enum variants, fields, and functions listed here must be public; derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq on public types. Do not use inner attributes or inner doc comments.

R2. API: pub enum SplitError { Nul { pos: usize }, TrailingEscape { pos: usize }, UnterminatedSingle { pos: usize }, UnterminatedDouble { pos: usize } }. pub fn split(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, SplitError>. All SplitError positions are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets in the original input, including positions after multibyte characters.

R3. Before any parsing, reject the first U+0000 in the entire input with Nul at its byte offset. This preflight error outranks all syntax errors, even ones earlier in the input. Environment strings (when present) are not included in this preflight.

R4. Only ASCII space, tab, CR, and LF separate words outside quotes. Other Unicode whitespace is ordinary word text. Repeated separators produce no empty words; empty input or only separators yields an empty vector.

R5. Outside quotes, ordinary characters append to the current word. Adjacent bare, quoted, escaped, and expanded fragments concatenate without introducing word boundaries.

R6. Unescaped single quote opens single quoting. All characters until the next single quote are literal, including backslashes, double quotes, dollar signs, LF and backticks; the delimiters are removed.

R7. Unescaped double quote opens double quoting. Single quotes inside double quotes are literal. Double-quote delimiters are removed; separators inside double quotes are literal.

R8. An opening quote activates a word even when it contributes no text. Thus empty quotes produce an empty word; adjacent empty quotes produce one empty word.

R9. Outside quotes, backslash followed by a scalar other than LF removes the backslash and appends that scalar literally, even when it is a quote, separator, dollar sign or backslash.

R10. Outside quotes, backslash immediately followed by LF removes both as a line continuation. The pair alone does not activate a word and cannot introduce a separator. Backslash CR is an escaped literal CR; a following LF is still a separator.

R11. Inside double quotes, backslash removes itself only before double quote, backslash, dollar sign, or LF. In the first three cases append the next scalar literally. For LF append nothing. Before any other scalar keep the backslash and process the next scalar normally inside the same double quotes.

R12. A backslash at end of input outside quotes or inside double quotes gives TrailingEscape at that backslash. Inside single quotes it is literal, so an unclosed single quote instead gives UnterminatedSingle.

R13. End of input inside a quote gives UnterminatedSingle or UnterminatedDouble at the opening delimiter of that currently open quote, unless R12 applies. Quote positions are not word-start positions.

R14. After the NUL preflight, scan left to right and return the first encountered error. At EOF a trailing escape takes precedence over an unclosed double quote. No partial words are returned on error.

R15. There are no comments, operators, tilde expansion, glob expansion or shell execution. Characters such as #, ;, |, &, parentheses and = are ordinary text unless a later clause explicitly assigns them meaning.

R16. When a literal scalar is appended, preserve its UTF-8 encoding exactly; do not normalize, trim, or change case.

R17. A successful split returns words in source order, with all delimiters and consumed escape characters removed according to these rules.

R18. Dollar signs and backticks are ordinary text; no variable expansion or command substitution recognition occurs.

R19. All wildcard characters are ordinary preserved text.
